record.original_question: Let r > 0 and let S be a sphere of radius r. Find a curve of minimal length that starts at the center of S and meets every plane tangent to S.

evidence.quote: Prenons le même problème dans l’espace. Quelle serait la courbe de longueur minimale, issue du centre d’une sphère de rayon r fixé, qui rencontrerait tout plan tangent à la sphère ?
Il y a bien des propositions de courbes remplissant la condition imposée (toucher tout plan tangent à la sphère),... mais aucune démonstration mathématique n’est là pour assurer l’optimalité.
Parmi les trajectoires du style de celles proposées dans la Figure 7, ce qu’on a trouvé de mieux est de longueur ≃ 13,66 r.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $r>0$ and let $S\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be a sphere of radius $r$ with center $O$. A rectifiable curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^3$ is said to "hit every tangent plane of $S$" if for every plane $\Pi\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ that is tangent to $S$, the image of $\gamma$ meets $\Pi$. Assume in addition that $\gamma(0)=O$. Determine the infimum of the lengths of all such curves $\gamma$, and exhibit a curve attaining this infimum (or prove that none exists).
artifact.status_search_result: The three-dimensional shortest "tangent-plane–hitting" curve issuing from the center of a sphere appears to remain open. The closely related closed-curve inspection problem for a sphere (Zalgaller's conjecture, with conjectured optimum 4π for the unit sphere) has been studied by Ghomi and Wenk, but the variant with one endpoint fixed at the center is not known to have been solved; the best known candidate trajectories have length approximately 13.66 r.

status_evidence.title: Shortest Closed Curve to Inspect a Sphere — Ghomi & Wenk
status_evidence.snippet: Shortest closed inspection curves of the unit sphere; Zalgaller's conjecture about length 4π for closed curves whose convex hull contains the sphere.
status_evidence.claim: The related closed-curve inspection problem for a sphere has been investigated, but the variant starting at the center remains a separate (open) optimization question.
